name: issue_827_hot_day_deadband_cleared_escalates
description: Companion to issue_827_hot_day_dawn_dip_within_deadband_no_escalate.json: proves that once a hot day's below-floor breach genuinely clears comfort_deadband_hot_f (default 5.0F), the family DOES escalate to heat once sustain-confirmed -- the wide hot-day deadband tolerates a modest dip but is not a blanket suppression of the safety backstop. A severe breach (well past 5F) is a real floor defense case regardless of day type.
source: Issue #827 Design table, deadband table 'Hot' row -- companion positive case to the within-deadband negative control.
notes: (a) Scenario effectiveness (revert-test): if comfort_deadband_hot_f were misconfigured/clamped to an unreasonably large value (e.g. the clamp's upper bound 8.0F raised or removed so a breach like this scenario's 7F never clears it), the final assertion (comfort_family=heating) would FAIL -- proving this scenario genuinely depends on the deadband being clamped to a bounded, real value, not an unbounded 'never escalate on a hot day' suppression.

(b) Docs<->production alignment: docs/08-COMPUTATION-REFERENCE.md #6f documents the deadband table's 'Hot' row (5.0F default, clamped [2,8]) and this scenario as its test reference for the escalate-past-deadband case, paired with the dawn-dip negative control.

(c) Occupant experience: a hot day's wide deadband tolerates a modest dip, but a home that has genuinely dropped 7F below its comfort floor overnight (a real cold snap, not a transient morning chill) still needs active defense -- otherwise the home could coast arbitrarily cold on a day CA expects to need cooling later, leaving occupants cold for hours before the day's own warming ever arrives.

Deliberately uses the SAME day_type/config shape as issue_827_hot_day_dawn_dip_within_deadband_no_escalate.json (comfort_heat=68, day_type='hot') -- only the indoor trajectory differs (7F breach here vs. 3F there), making the two scenarios a direct before/after-the-deadband-line comparison pair.

events.note: A genuine cold snap: indoor drops to 61F, 7F below comfort_heat(68) -- clears comfort_deadband_hot_f (default 5.0F, clamped [2,8]) with margin.
First below-deadband tick. Fallback candidate arms, not yet sustain-confirmed (elapsed 0s < 90s). Stays 'cooling' this tick.
120s later (>90s). First-ever transition for this engine (cold start, no dwell gate). Sustain-confirmed: comfort family escalates to heating, commands heat at comfort_heat(68).

assertions.reason: Baseline: hot day, indoor within band -- comfort band arms normally at the ceiling.
A 7F breach clears comfort_deadband_hot_f (5.0F) with margin -- once sustain-confirmed, the family escalates to heating despite the hot-day classification.
The escalated mode is a real climate.set_temperature/set_hvac_mode call at comfort_heat, not merely an internal flag.

verdict.summary: A hot-day breach that genuinely clears comfort_deadband_hot_f (5.0F default) escalates to heat once sustain-confirmed, proving the wide hot-day deadband is a bounded tolerance, not a blanket suppression of the safety backstop.
verdict.observed_behavior: Indoor drops to 61F (7F below the 68F floor, past the 5F hot-day deadband) -- comfort family escalates to heating at 06:17:00 once sustain-confirmed.
verdict.expected_behavior: The hot-day deadband tolerates a modest dip but not a genuine, severe cold snap -- once cleared, the same sustain-confirmed escalation mechanism every other day type uses applies here too.
